03800.HK-B1.rationale: The threshold tests reproducible full-size improvements that shorten qualification cycles and raise saleable manufacturing yield.

03800.HK-B2.rationale: The threshold requires sustained cost, yield, or quality gains that create a durable ASP-cost spread or better product mix.

03800.HK-B3.rationale: The threshold tests incremental solar investment that absorbs photovoltaic supply and improves polysilicon industry utilization.

03800.HK-B4.rationale: The threshold tests competitors reaching scaled cost or quality parity and winning customers, weakening pricing, share, and margins.

AG1-B1.rationale: The threshold requires broad deployment that reduces inspection time or rework without increasing customer claims.

AG1-B2.rationale: The threshold tests higher realized GPU and inventory velocity without increased markdowns or loss-making cohorts.

AG1-B3.rationale: The threshold requires agents to reduce human touches and response times while preserving conversion and document quality.

AG1-B4.rationale: The threshold tests higher financing approval or attachment with stable credit losses, funding, and regulatory compliance.

AG1-B5.rationale: The threshold tests rival capability parity followed by weaker conversion, dealer activity, or higher acquisition costs.

AMD-B1.rationale: The threshold requires paid production deployments and customer expansion at competitive workload economics.

AMD-B2.rationale: The threshold tests both outcomes, but near-day-zero production support would strengthen Instinct qualification, demand, and pricing.

AMD-B3.rationale: The threshold tests custom accelerators absorbing production capacity and reducing planned Instinct orders.

AMD-B4.rationale: The threshold tests supply allocations that defer Helios shipments or raise unit costs enough to compress gross margin.

AMD-B5.rationale: The threshold tests export rules that block or delay sales or impose costly product redesigns and charges.

AMZN-B1.rationale: The threshold requires AI demand to become billable capacity at utilization and pricing sufficient to cover the capital base.

AMZN-B2.rationale: The threshold tests verified Trainium workload economics and broad production adoption.

AMZN-B3.rationale: The threshold requires sustained production-agent usage that drives measurable consumption and retention across AWS services.

AMZN-B4.rationale: The threshold tests durable incremental purchases or retention after all cannibalization and operating costs.

AMZN-B5.rationale: The threshold requires audited operating improvements at scale while preserving customer experience, safety, and compliance.

AVGO-B1.rationale: The threshold requires custom-silicon wins to reach profitable volume production and retain content across generations.

AVGO-B2.rationale: The threshold tests volume deployment of Broadcom-based Ethernet with sustained revenue from greater bandwidth and optical content.

AVGO-B3.rationale: The threshold requires production AI on VCF to generate attributable renewals, expansion, and durable margin.

AVGO-B4.rationale: The threshold anchors downside on efficiency outpacing demand and reducing or delaying aggregate accelerator and networking deployments.

AXON-B1.rationale: The threshold tests broad agency adoption with persistent productivity gains and software gross profit exceeding governance costs.

AXON-B2.rationale: The threshold requires reliable, governed operational outcomes that support expanded deployments across jurisdictions.

AXON-B3.rationale: The threshold tests scalable approved drone deployments with reliable outcomes and accompanying recurring software economics.

COHR-B1.rationale: The threshold requires optical link growth to exceed price erosion while new capacity achieves acceptable yields.

COHR-B2.rationale: The threshold tests high-volume CPO production with economically meaningful company content after pluggable cannibalization.

COHR-B3.rationale: The threshold requires a major operator to deploy optical circuit switching at scale with company production volume.

COHR-B4.rationale: The threshold tests optical demand falling below committed capacity and causing an unabsorbed capacity gap.

COHR-B5.rationale: The threshold requires AI-related equipment investment to expand categories containing meaningful company content and offset other weakness.

DDOG-B1.rationale: The threshold tests incremental paid AI-observability usage and cross-sell with revenue exceeding infrastructure costs.

DDOG-B2.rationale: The threshold requires broad paid agent usage, persistent resolution gains, low incident rates, and costs below revenue.

DDOG-B3.rationale: The threshold tests sustained incremental paid telemetry and module adoption without platform displacement.

DDOG-B4.rationale: The threshold tests lower-cost alternatives causing sustained customer losses or weaker expansion.

DDOG-B5.rationale: The threshold tests both cost directions, but costs outgrowing monetized AI usage would compress gross margin.

DUOL-B1.rationale: The threshold requires conversion, retention, and pricing gains to exceed inference costs and Max-tier cannibalization.

DUOL-B2.rationale: The threshold tests falling cost per successful interaction without sacrificing response quality or reliability.

DUOL-B3.rationale: The threshold requires more approved and effective course units per expert-hour with stable quality and efficacy.

DUOL-B4.rationale: The threshold tests lower-priced general assistants achieving comparable efficacy and sustained learner retention.

DUOL-B5.rationale: The threshold tests scaled errors or restrictions that damage retention, product use, or test recognition.

GOOGL-B1.rationale: The threshold requires AI activity and monetization to exceed inference costs and conventional-search cannibalization.

GOOGL-B2.rationale: The threshold tests rivals taking valuable activity and advertising budgets or weakening Google's distribution and data advantages.

GOOGL-B3.rationale: The threshold requires recurring production consumption and capacity returns above depreciation, energy, and support costs.

GOOGL-B4.rationale: The threshold requires efficiency and utilization gains to outrun workload and replacement costs, improving margins and capital efficiency.

GOOGL-B5.rationale: The threshold equally permits paid Cloud security adoption or damaging incidents, but adoption is more specific to the named security-product exposure.

GRND-B1.rationale: The threshold requires improved connection outcomes and retained usage to convert into incremental paid adoption or retention.

GRND-B2.rationale: The threshold requires durable reductions in AI interaction or product-cycle costs after added infrastructure and staffing expenses.

GRND-B3.rationale: The threshold tests lost user time, connection intent, or willingness to pay due to substitute assistants.

GRND-B4.rationale: The threshold requires lower verified harm and moderation workload while preserving user trust and legal validity.

HNGE-B1.rationale: The threshold requires broad, clinically validated gains in member outcomes or engagement without higher safety-event rates.

HNGE-B2.rationale: The threshold requires automation to reduce low-value clinician work while maintaining or improving outcomes, satisfaction, and safety.

HNGE-B3.rationale: The threshold tests rivals winning RFPs or forcing discounts through credible outcome parity, weakening differentiation and pricing.

HNGE-B4.rationale: The threshold tests incidents or new requirements that delay launches, increase review burdens, or impair retention and procurement.

HOOD-B1.rationale: The threshold requires sustained retention, deposit, or ARPU gains whose gross profit exceeds AI and compliance costs.

HOOD-B2.rationale: The threshold requires agentic accounts to add funded customers, deposits, trades, or spend with costs below monetization.

HOOD-B3.rationale: The threshold tests customer losses, complaints, enforcement, redesign, or Gold churn from model errors.

HOOD-B4.rationale: The threshold requires lower investigation time, backlog, or staffing without worse fraud or regulatory outcomes.

HOOD-B5.rationale: The threshold can capture either cheaper off-app volume or weaker Gold attachment and trade economics, but the latter most directly tests agent disintermediation.

HUT-B1.rationale: The threshold requires executable leases at returns above all-in development, financing, and residual-risk costs.

HUT-B2.rationale: The threshold requires density or tenant-demand gains to exceed redesign, equipment, and delay costs.

HUT-B3.rationale: The threshold tests efficiency reducing required compute faster than workloads grow, weakening leasing and renewals.

HUT-B4.rationale: The threshold centers on counterparty concentration that can impair contracted economics unless payment support and site reusability mitigate it.

IFX-B1.rationale: The threshold requires scaled platform shipments, rising megawatts, retained power content, and a timely capacity ramp supporting revenue and margin growth.

IFX-B2.rationale: The threshold tests multi-quarter declines in deployed megawatts and orders while manufacturing capacity continues ramping.

IFX-B3.rationale: The threshold requires permitted power projects to reach procurement and include the company's components.

IFX-B4.rationale: The threshold requires models to fit MCU constraints and multiple OEMs to advance to serial production.

IFX-B5.rationale: The threshold requires serial robot production and multi-function bill-of-material wins, supporting revenue and product mix.

INPST-B1.rationale: The threshold requires sustained utilization or peak-handling gains without increasing capital expenditure per parcel.

INPST-B2.rationale: The threshold requires production-route cost or throughput improvements while service quality is maintained.

INPST-B3.rationale: The threshold requires more contacts resolved without humans while complaint, repeat-contact, refund, and error rates hold or improve.

INPST-B4.rationale: The threshold requires faster sales workflows to produce retained merchants and incremental profitable parcel volume.

INPST-B5.rationale: The threshold tests sustained downtime, data compromise, parcel loss, regulatory action, or significant SLA penalties.

INTC-B1.rationale: The threshold requires rising CPU demand per AI system without offsetting share or pricing losses.

INTC-B2.rationale: The threshold tests a sustained migration of cloud workloads away from x86, reducing server revenue and margin.

INTC-B3.rationale: The threshold requires multiple external designs to reach sustained production at competitive yield, pricing, and returns.

INTC-B4.rationale: The threshold requires widely used local applications to drive measurable PC replacement demand and pricing premiums.

INTC-B5.rationale: The threshold requires production-scale custom awards whose economics exceed lost standard-processor contribution.

IREN-B1.rationale: The threshold requires signed demand to cover commissioned capacity at attractive pricing with durable high utilization.

IREN-B2.rationale: The threshold tests efficiency or custom silicon outpacing workload growth and weakening external GPU demand.

IREN-B3.rationale: The threshold tests facility-design shortfalls or cooling, networking, and electrical bottlenecks that delay contracted deployments.

IREN-B4.rationale: The threshold requires customers to pay for managed services while performance and uptime hold at scale.

IREN-B5.rationale: The threshold tests new accelerators obsoleting the existing fleet before contracted revenue amortizes it.

KSPI-B1.rationale: The threshold requires sustained incremental transactions or retention after serving costs without higher complaints or harmful outcomes.

KSPI-B2.rationale: The threshold requires broad merchant adoption to lift conversion or advertising spend with revenue above model and remediation costs.

KSPI-B3.rationale: The threshold requires materially deployed models to deliver superior out-of-sample credit-loss and fraud performance.

KSPI-B4.rationale: The threshold requires sustained engagement and contribution-profit gains culminating in durable positive adjusted EBITDA.

KSPI-B5.rationale: The threshold tests customer selection shifting to unaffiliated agents, weakening discovery, take rate, and customer ownership.

LITE-B1.rationale: Sustained high-speed volume orders supported by capacity and yields would increase shipments and product mix.

LITE-B2.rationale: Expanded CPO deployments with retained laser content exceeding lost pluggable contribution would increase net optical revenue.

LITE-B3.rationale: Backlog conversion, repeat orders and reliable deployments would establish a new systems revenue stream.

LITE-B4.rationale: Production qualification and committed volumes sufficient to justify investment would open a billable VCSEL market.

LITE-B5.rationale: Falling optical orders, weaker pricing and unchanged capacity commitments would reduce revenue, margins and utilization.

LKNCY-B1.rationale: Meaningful agent-originated orders with higher retention or contribution profit would improve demand and customer economics.

LKNCY-B2.rationale: Persistent reductions in forecast error, waste and stockouts would improve availability, margins and working capital.

LKNCY-B3.rationale: Higher repeat rates and contribution margins without disproportionate complexity would improve product-launch economics.

LKNCY-B4.rationale: Lower labor and downtime per order without more quality failures would improve store-level margins.

LKNCY-B5.rationale: Higher utilization and lower per-ton costs sufficient to earn acceptable returns would improve manufacturing economics.

LMND-B1.rationale: More verified end-to-end automation without higher leakage or complaints would lower handling costs and improve service.

LMND-B2.rationale: Improved cohort-adjusted underwriting and acquisition economics would raise gross profit per exposure and acquisition dollar.

LMND-B3.rationale: Scaled autonomous-mile cohorts with mature loss performance and adequate unit economics would support profitable share gains.

LMND-B4.rationale: Fraud losses and manual-review rates rising faster than premiums would erase automation savings and weaken profitability.

META-B1.rationale: Sustained engagement and impressions without equivalent trust or retention declines would increase advertising revenue.

META-B2.rationale: Incremental advertiser returns and demand exceeding compute costs would increase advertising revenue and profit.

META-B3.rationale: The more exposure-specific threshold tests efficiency, utilization and custom-silicon gains that lower costs and improve returns.

META-B4.rationale: Broad repeat usage, paid value and declining cost per completed task would create durable agent revenue.

META-B5.rationale: Sustained shipments and upgrades with positive contribution would grow hardware revenue and narrow segment losses.

MRVL-B1.rationale: Additional custom-silicon programs reaching sustained qualified production would increase unit and design revenue.

MRVL-B2.rationale: Qualified systems, purchase commitments and production revenue would expand custom-silicon and interconnect sales.

MRVL-B3.rationale: Volume adoption with rising content per cluster would increase port value, mix and data-center revenue.

MRVL-B4.rationale: Major production deployments and meaningful socket wins would add switching and connectivity revenue.

MRVL-B5.rationale: Lower infrastructure purchases, delayed clusters or insourced programs would reduce revenue and worsen capacity absorption.

MSFT-B1.rationale: Billable workload growth, utilization and pricing exceeding infrastructure costs would improve cloud profit and cash returns.

MSFT-B2.rationale: Production deployments that lift revenue and retention above serving costs would increase recurring gross profit.

MSFT-B3.rationale: Application replacement, weaker renewals and insufficient offsetting cloud consumption would reduce application gross profit.

MSFT-B4.rationale: The more direct threshold branch is substantial workload migration away from Azure, which would reduce cloud demand.

MSFT-B5.rationale: The product-specific threshold tests governance and security becoming decisive paid features that strengthen revenue and retention.

MU-B1.rationale: Accelerator and HBM-content growth outpacing supply while qualifications persist would increase HBM volume and mix.

MU-B2.rationale: HBM capacity consumption exceeding replacement bit growth would tighten conventional DRAM supply and support pricing and margins.

MU-B3.rationale: Agent-driven server and memory growth outpacing efficiency gains would increase conventional memory demand.

MU-B4.rationale: AI-related NAND consumption and premium SSD adoption exceeding supply growth would improve revenue, mix and pricing.

MU-B5.rationale: Memory requirements falling faster than AI workloads grow would weaken demand, utilization and pricing.

NTSK-B1.rationale: Paid production adoption generating measurable expansion or competitive wins would increase recurring revenue and mix.

NTSK-B2.rationale: Meaningful production agent traffic through interoperable low-latency controls would support adoption and revenue expansion.

NTSK-B3.rationale: Production automation whose accuracy and throughput exceed review and error costs would increase ARR and service efficiency.

NTSK-B4.rationale: Purchasing differentiation and network savings exceeding capacity costs would improve wins, retention and margins.

NTSK-B5.rationale: Buyer preference for bundled controls or restricted platform access would slow recurring-revenue growth and weaken differentiation.

NVDA-B1.rationale: Compute spending growth exceeding price-performance gains without material migration would increase Data Center revenue and gross profit.

NVDA-B2.rationale: Sustained agent token volumes with usage expanding faster than hardware efficiency would drive recurring infrastructure demand.

NVDA-B3.rationale: Compute per useful task falling faster than usage expands would reduce accelerator requirements and platform spending.

NVDA-B4.rationale: Competing accelerators winning material production deployments would cause revenue-share loss and margin pressure.

NVDA-B5.rationale: Broad restrictions that prevent demand redirection without price, timing or margin loss would reduce revenue and profitability.

OMDA-B1.rationale: Sustained incremental retention and lower care-team hours without added safety issues would improve revenue and margins.

OMDA-B2.rationale: Measurable clinical and medical-cost improvements across cohorts would strengthen buyer ROI, renewals, and revenue.

OMDA-B3.rationale: A systematic care error, serious incident, or regulatory restriction would raise costs and impair retention and growth.

OMDA-B4.rationale: Weaker renewals, lower prices, or channel insourcing by adequate competing AI products would erode revenue and differentiation.

OSCR-B1.rationale: Broad Oswell use that reduces contact or utilization costs without worse outcomes would improve retention and unit economics.

OSCR-B2.rationale: Service savings exceeding model and oversight costs while preserving quality would improve operating leverage.

OSCR-B3.rationale: Recurring high-stakes guidance errors or inadequate controls would create legal, regulatory, utilization, and attrition costs.

OSCR-B4.rationale: Meaningful enrollment volume and higher conversion or product attachment would increase premium and adjacent revenue.

OSCR-B5.rationale: Financially visible contract wins, client lives, and services revenue would expand growth and margins.

PANW-B1.rationale: Production agent adoption and dedicated independent-control budgets would expand subscriptions, contract breadth, and retention.

PANW-B2.rationale: Superior detection and response at lower operating cost amid stronger attacks would increase demand and platform consolidation.

PANW-B3.rationale: Customer preference for consistent third-party controls across heterogeneous AI stacks would support differentiation and pricing.

PANW-B4.rationale: Demand for enforceable agent controls beyond native tools would create incremental subscription spend and platform adoption.

PANW-B5.rationale: Native controls reaching comparable enterprise efficacy would compress pricing and reduce the platform's addressable scope.

PSTG-B1.rationale: Production deployments that measurably improve accelerator utilization would increase product revenue, ARR, and installed-base expansion.

PSTG-B2.rationale: Paid production adoption with incremental attach or expansion would increase recurring revenue and software mix.

PSTG-B3.rationale: Sustained hyperscaler production volume and additional customer validation would generate substantial product, licensing, and support revenue.

PSTG-B4.rationale: Persistent shipment constraints or input-cost inflation exceeding pricing benefits would compress revenue and gross margin.

PSTG-B5.rationale: Declining shared-storage content per AI cluster and orders lagging compute growth would weaken adoption and product mix.

RBRK-B1.rationale: Production customers purchasing, renewing, and expanding Agent Cloud would increase subscription ARR and net retention.

RBRK-B2.rationale: AI-driven threats shifting enterprise spending toward independently validated recovery would increase core subscription demand.

RBRK-B3.rationale: Shorter recovery times and lower manual effort without added failures would improve win rates, retention, pricing, and support economics.

RBRK-B4.rationale: Paid production AI workflows and expansion of protected datasets would increase ARR and net retention.

RBRK-B5.rationale: Native tools that meet cross-platform needs or restrict access would displace Agent Cloud and weaken ARR.

RDDT-B1.rationale: New or renewed agreements that materially add other revenue would improve consolidated growth and margins.

RDDT-B2.rationale: Unoffset declines in search-referred users and ad impressions would reduce advertising inventory and acquisition efficiency.

RDDT-B3.rationale: Sustained gains in retention, contribution, or monetizable sessions net of serving costs would improve advertising economics.

RDDT-B4.rationale: Repeatable advertiser-return improvements that raise spend and ARPU net of costs would increase revenue and operating leverage.

RDDT-B5.rationale: Synthetic abuse that reduces legitimate participation, advertiser confidence, or data reliability would raise costs and weaken the platform moat.

SNDK-B1.rationale: Sustained production qualifications and outsized Datacenter exabyte growth would increase higher-value enterprise revenue and gross margin.

SNDK-B2.rationale: HBF meeting technical requirements and entering a production roadmap would create premium memory revenue.

SNDK-B3.rationale: Recurring high-capacity SSD deployments based on operating-cost savings would expand addressable exabytes and revenue.

SNDK-B4.rationale: Higher standard device capacities and qualified socket wins without offsetting price declines would raise revenue per device.

SNDK-B5.rationale: Bit-supply growth exceeding demand would raise inventories, weaken NAND pricing, and compress gross margin.

TSM-B1.rationale: Sustained AI production orders filling incremental advanced-node capacity at attractive pricing would raise revenue and gross profit.

TSM-B2.rationale: Retaining packaging share while scaling capacity without persistent yield or cycle-time penalties would improve revenue and mix.

TSM-B3.rationale: Efficiency outpacing AI usage growth and leaving committed capacity underutilized would reduce wafer demand and returns.

TSM-B4.rationale: Incremental AI silicon area and advanced-node adoption exceeding device and compute offsets would increase wafer demand and mix.

TSM-B5.rationale: Restrictions on major products or equipment and underutilized localized fabs would weaken demand, margins, and capital returns.

XMTR-B1.rationale: Sustained conversion and support-cost improvements without added quality failures would increase volume and marketplace efficiency.

XMTR-B2.rationale: Realized margin, delivery, and remediation gains across meaningful volume would improve marketplace economics.

XMTR-B3.rationale: Native integrations generating attributable order volume at scale would increase enterprise revenue and repeat spending.

XMTR-B4.rationale: Sustained recurring data-center orders at acceptable realized margins would increase marketplace revenue and gross profit.

XMTR-B5.rationale: Comparable competitor fulfillment accompanied by deteriorating repeat rates, pricing spreads, or supplier participation would pressure growth and margins.
